chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is Umar ibn Muslim doing?' I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! He has devoted himself to worship and abandoned trade.' He said: 'Woe to him! Does he not know that one who abandons the seeking (of livelihood) will not have his supplications answered?'

Indeed, a group from among the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when the verse was revealed: 'And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, and He will provide for him from where he does not reckon,' they locked their doors and devoted themselves to worship, saying: 'We have been provided for.'

This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and he sent for them and said: 'What drove you to what you have done?' They said: 'O Messenger of God! Our provisions were guaranteed for us, so we devoted ourselves to worship.' He said: 'Indeed whoever does that, his supplications will not be answered. You must seek (your livelihood).'

key_terms.الطَّلَب: Seeking/pursuit of livelihood; active effort to earn one's sustenance
key_terms.تَارِكَ الطَّلَبِ: One who abandons the seeking of livelihood; condemned for passivity
key_terms.لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُ: His supplications are not answered; spiritual consequence of abandoning work
key_terms.مَخْرَجاً: A way out/an outlet; God's promise of relief to the God-fearing
key_terms.وَيْحَهُ: Expression of pity or rebuke: 'woe to him', indicating strong disapproval

ai.seo_question: Does abandoning work for worship mean supplications will not be answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rebukes the misunderstanding that Quranic promises of divine provision excuse abandoning worldly work. Through a historical precedent from the Prophet's time, the Imam clarifies that even though God promises sustenance to the God-fearing, this divine promise requires active effort — one who abandons seeking livelihood will not have his supplications accepted. The hadith addresses a recurring misreading of Quran 65:2-3 that led some early Muslims to withdraw from trade and commerce, believing reliance on God meant passivity.
